problem: A particle $P$ of mass $1\,kg$ moves along the $x$-axis under the action of a force of magnitude $6\sqrt{x}\,N$ acting in the direction of increasing $x.$ Given that $x$ is measured in meters, and the particle has velocity $v=2\sqrt{2}\,m/s$ at $x=1,$ calculate the velocity of the particle at $x=4.$

feedback.problem: A particle $P$ of mass $1.5\,kg$ moves along the $x$-axis under the action of a resultant force. The particle's velocity is $5t\,m/s,$ where $t\ge 0$ is the time in seconds. Calculate the work done by the force between the times $t=2\,s$ and $t=4\,s.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The work-energy principle states that the work done by a resultant force on a particle equals the change in the particle's kinetic energy. That is,

$$
W=Δ\,\text{KE}
$$

where the change in kinetic energy of a particle is given by

$$
Δ\,\text{KE}=\frac{1}{2}m{v}_{1}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}m{v}_{0}^{2}
$$

and $m$ is the particle's mass, ${v}_{0}$ is its initial velocity, and ${v}_{1}$ is its final velocity.

The particle's velocity is given by $v(t)=5t,$ where $t$ is time in seconds. So, the particle's initial velocity, at $t=2$, is

$$
{v}_{0}=v(2)=5(2)=10\,m/s,
$$

and final velocity, at $t=4$, is

$$
{v}_{1}=v(4)=5(4)=20\,m/s.
$$

Therefore, by the work-energy principle, the work done by the force between these times is

$$
\begin{aligned}W & =Δ\,\text{KE} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 1.5\cdot (20)^{2}-\frac{1}{2}\cdot 1.5\cdot (10)^{2} \\  & =300-75 \\  & =225\,J.\end{aligned}
$$
